html:
The Shiwiar are a small Indigenous people of the Amazon lowlands of eastern Ecuador and northern Peru, along the Corrientes and upper Pastaza rivers. They speak a Chicham (Jivaroan) language close to that of the Achuar, and are related to the Shuar and Awajún.

Like other Chicham peoples, they lived in scattered households rather than villages, growing manioc in forest gardens and hunting with blowguns. The Chicham peoples kept their independence against both the Inca and the Spanish. Since the late 1900s oil drilling in the Pastaza basin has been the main threat to their land.
